memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron about the Israelites and Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he commanded them to bring the Israelites out of Egypt." - Exodus 6:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses has just listed his inadequacy again. God's response is simply to issue the command again.

There is no argument here, no lengthy reassurance, no fresh miracle. God does not debate Moses' self-assessment. He commissions him and moves on.

Sometimes that is exactly what we need. Not more reassurance, but a clear word to get moving. We can spend years processing our inadequacy while the task waits. At some point, feelings must follow obedience rather than lead it.

Notice too that God addresses Moses and Aaron together. The commission is shared. God knows we obey better in company than alone.

There is something quietly reassuring in this verse. God did not withdraw the calling because Moses hesitated. He did not find a more confident candidate. He simply repeated Himself.

If God has made something clear to you and you have been stalling in self-doubt, the word may not change. It may simply come again.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God made clear that I am still debating with myself?
2. Am I waiting to feel capable before I obey?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for not giving up on me when I hesitate. Give me grace to obey even before my feelings catch up. Amen.
